1. SMALLEST DESIGN

- Drop `tab: none`. The GCT round 2 problem was that one screen per scene made the tab bar busy. `screen "Name" from Data` already "never has a tab" and solves row-detail screens. For non-row secondary views opened by a button (like `"About"`), v0.2/v0.3 already has `dialog`. Adding `tab: none` creates a second kind of untabbed view with its own Back-button navigation stack. If you keep untabbed non-row screens at all, make "no tab + Back button" automatic whenever a screen is not the first screen and is targetable by `opens screen`, instead of adding the keyword `tab: none`.
- Merge `play-view` and `stage-read` (or make `stage-read` include `play-view`). In Section 2's example, `screen "Scene"` puts `play-view "{row.text}"` and `stage-read "{row.text}"` one after the other. In Section 5, `stage-read` "reads the scene line by line... and highlights the line being read." Either `stage-read` draws the script itself (so putting both on a screen renders the play twice) or `stage-read` magically reaches into a sibling `play-view` DOM node. Having `stage-read "{row.text}"` render the Diana-format script plus the Play/Stop bar and line highlighting (while `play-view "{row.text}"` renders it without audio) removes the duplicate declaration on every scene screen, or lets one element (`play-view` with an optional `@stage-read` role) do both.
- Keep `read: private`, `from Data`, and `{row.field}`. `read: own` is live in v0.3 for host-approved `status` workflows, so `read: private` is the minimal way to exclude the host.

2. AMBIGUITIES

- `"play-view "{row.text}""` followed by `"stage-read "{row.text}""` (Section 2) vs. `"A Play button reads the scene line by line, each character in its own voice, and highlights the line being read"` (Section 5): It is unclear whether `stage-read` renders its own script view or attaches to a `play-view` on the same screen. An AI builder following Section 2 will always emit both.
- `"a line in capitals by itself (OLDER ERIC) is a character cue, and the lines under it, up to a blank line, are that character's speech"` vs. `"ACT ONE, SCENE TWO, is a heading"` and `"technical cues (lights, sound, blackout) at the margin"` (Section 5): All three are lines in capitals by themselves. Without a deterministic precedence rule, `stage-read` will treat `BLACKOUT` or `ACT ONE, SCENE TWO` as character names and speak the lines under them in a character voice.
- `"The page sends the row's address and a line number"` (Section 5): "Line number" could mean newline index in `{row.field}`, parsed speech-block index, or spoken-line index skipping headings and stage directions. Client highlighter and server parser will drift unless this is defined.
- `"It shows a Back button that returns to the screen that opened it"` (Section 1) vs. `"screen "Scene" from scenes shows one row of scenes: the row that opened it. It never has a tab"` (Section 2): Section 2 says a `from Data` screen has no tab, not that it has `tab: none`, leaving it ambiguous whether `from Data` screens also get a Back button.
- `"Both live in the component library package packages/soma-play and take a scene's text, usually a {row.field} on a screen that shows one row"` vs. `"The text must be a {row.field} of the screen's row"` (Section 5): Does `play-view` accept literal text or `stub` fields while `stage-read` requires `data`-backed `{row.field}`?
- `"This check applies to descriptions whose version is "0.2" or later"` (Section 4): Retroactively making unknown `{tokens}` a parse error in `"0.2"` and `"0.3"` breaks existing saved descriptions and undo/redo history from GCT rounds 1 and 2. Apply the error only to `"0.4"` and later (or warn on `"0.2"`/`"0.3"`).
- `"Only the author removes a private row"` (Section 3 and route table): v0.3 requires a visible `removes from Name` action and `status == "pending"` for non-hosts. For `read: private` (and data without `status`), it is unclear whether a visible `removes from Name` button is still required on the screen/list.

3. SECURITY AND ABUSE HOLES

- Host-only screen escape via `opens screen`: v0.3 says `"a host-only screen may not open a dialog that everyone receives."` It did not mention screens because all v0.3 screens had tabs. In v0.4, if a `requires: host` screen opens a `screen "Name" from Data` (or `tab: none` screen) that omits `requires: host`, `/current` strips the host-only screen but sends the detail screen AND its `Data` block to everyone, bypassing v0.3's rule that host-only data must declare `read: own`.
- `/stage-read` missing screen-visibility check: `POST /stage-read` checks that `"the live version must have a stage-read of that field on a screen from that data"`, not that the caller can see that screen. If `stage-read` is on a `requires: host` screen over readable data, a non-host can still call `/stage-read`.
- Burning the 50k-character ElevenLabs budget in one request or burst:
  1. "A spend check runs on every line" measures lines or checks allowance without bounding line length; a user who can `adds to scenes` can submit a single `"ERIC: <50,000 chars>"` line and drain the entire monthly budget in one call. Allowances must be counted in characters with a strict per-line and per-field character cap, deducted before calling ElevenLabs.
  2. Netlify Blobs is eventually consistent; 50 parallel `POST /stage-read` calls will all pass a non-atomic blob read before any write lands.
  3. Any signed-in user in an app with `adds to` + `stage-read` can paste arbitrary text into a new row and use `/stage-read` as a free TTS proxy.
- TTS cache cross-user oracle vs. edit invalidation: Puppet has no edit action—updating a scene means `removes from` + `adds to` (a new `rowId`). If the TTS cache is keyed by `rowId`, every scene revision re-bills every line. If keyed globally by `(voice, text)` and `"costs nothing"`, an attacker can test whether another writer's private play contains a suspected line by checking whether speaking it is fast and charges 0 allowance. Key the cache by `(authorId, voice, textHash)` or always charge the caller's daily allowance on another author's cache hit.
- Guessable IDs after privacy tightening: v0.3 only gave `read: own` rows unguessable IDs. If a collection starts public and later tightens to `read: own` or `read: private`, earlier rows keep sequential IDs. Every row in every collection must get an unguessable ID at creation, and `read: private` must explicitly require sign-in even on `publicRead` apps.
- Side-channel on `/stage-read` errors: `/stage-read` must verify read access to `rowId` before checking whether `line` exists or checking spend allowance, returning the identical not-found response so callers cannot probe line counts of private rows.
- Second-pass token expansion: When rendering `{row.field}` or `{form.Label}`, the renderer must never expand `{...}` tokens found inside stored row data.

RANKED CHANGES TO MAKE

1. Charge `/stage-read` allowances in characters (not lines), cap characters per line and per call, and rate-limit concurrent TTS calls per user/app so parallel requests cannot race Netlify Blobs and drain the 50k budget.
2. Extend v0.3's `requires: host` boundary rule to screens: a host-only screen/dialog may only open a `requires: host` screen/dialog, and non-host screens may not open host-only screens.
3. Require `POST /stage-read` to verify that the caller can see the `screen ... from Data` containing `stage-read` AND can read `rowId` (with sign-in required for `read: own`/`read: private` even on `publicRead` apps) before checking line bounds or spend.
4. Key the Stage Read audio cache by `(authorId, voiceId, textHash)` (or charge user allowance on cross-author hits) so replacing a row keeps the author's cache without creating a cross-writer text oracle.
5. Assign unguessable IDs to rows of all collections at creation so tightening privacy later never leaves old rows with guessable IDs, and ensure `{Name.count}` on `read: private` counts only the host's own rows for the host.
6. Merge `stage-read` with `play-view` (or state that `stage-read` renders the script itself) and define exact line-indexing and heading/cue precedence rules so `ACT ONE` and `BLACKOUT` are not spoken as characters.
7. Drop `tab: none` (use `dialog` for button-opened popups and `screen ... from Data` for untabbed row screens, with automatic Back button on `from Data` screens).
8. Apply the unknown-`{token}` parse error only to version `"0.4"` and later, and require single-pass token interpolation so `{tokens}` inside stored row values are never expanded.
9. Specify that deleting a `read: private` row (or any row without `status`) still requires a visible `removes from Name` action for the author, without checking `status == "pending"`.
